summary: This neighborhood story describes how the community is confronting the linked problems of substance abuse and mental health disorders, and the stigma that keeps people from seeking help. It covers local initiatives such as SMHIL, the school program "Mind Matters", police support for a rehabilitative approach, town halls, and alternative therapies. The note stresses cross-sector collaboration among law enforcement, educators, health professionals and community organizations.
one_line: A neighborhood effort led by the New Dawn Community Center, SMHIL and local schools tackles substance abuse and mental health stigma through collaboration.
key_facts: The New Dawn Community Center has become a crucial hub for people facing substance abuse and mental health disorders, with volunteers preparing for visitors every day for the past several months as of November 17, 2023.
The local health department released statistics on September 20, 2023 showing an alarming rise in reported substance abuse cases and mental health emergencies in the neighborhood.

Michael Jennings, a 38-year-old former construction worker, struggled with depression for years and turned to alcohol; he said at a support group on October 3, 2023, "It was the only thing that quieted the noise in my head."
The Substance and Mental Health Intervention League (SMHIL) was launched on September 15, 2023 under the leadership of Dr. Samantha Cho.
SMHIL works with community resource centers like New Dawn on workshops, counseling sessions and rehabilitation services, and partners with schools on early intervention programs.
Police data shared at a community forum on October 28, 2023 showed an uptick in drug-related offenses.
Officer James McKinnon, a 15-year veteran of the force, said, "We cannot arrest our way out of this problem."
The Riverside School District launched "Mind Matters" on September 25, 2023 to create open dialogue about mental health among students and teachers; its coordinator is Lauren Singh.
Town hall meetings, including one on November 5, 2023, aim to foster a stigma-free environment.
Maria Gonzales, a local librarian who has dealt with anxiety and substance dependency, shares her story and says, "Silence feeds the stigma."
Yoga, meditation and art therapy sessions are offered weekly at community centers as a holistic approach to healing.
Jaden Kim, a certified yoga instructor, spoke about the benefits of these practices during a guided session on December 10, 2023.
